--- FIVE WORST DEEP-DIVES ---

1. content/blog/supply-vs-delivery-charges-electricity.md — draft:true + canonical to the published 24-delivery-vs-supply post; the published post already carries alias '/blog/supply-vs-delivery-charges-electricity/', so this draft's slug would collide if ever rendered with --buildDrafts. Evidence: front matter reads `draft: true` and `canonical: "https://utilityexplained.com/blog/24-delivery-charge-vs-supply-charge-utility-bill/"`; the 24- post front matter contains `aliases: ["/blog/supply-vs-delivery-charges-electricity/"]`. Body is the weakest of the three drafts ('That split is real, and it is one of the fastest ways to make a bill feel less confusing.'). Recommendation: delete the file; the canonical target already covers the intent.

2. content/blog/how-to-read-your-utility-bill.md — the highest-search-volume query in this shard ('how to read your utility bill') is left as draft:true. Content quality is genuinely good (ordered steps, two tables, DOE PDF source), so this is an execution failure, not a content failure. Recommendation: set draft:false after checking no sibling page already occupies the /blog/how-to-read-your-utility-bill/ URL; add an annotated bill visual so the answer is visible fast.

3. content/blog/gas-customer-charge-explained.md — also draft:true. The tariff-first method is defensible, but 'How to Review a Gas Customer Charge' is a narrow, self-help framing that answers the query indirectly; and being unpublished it earns zero search exposure. Recommendation: publish (with the two DOE sources already listed) or remove-or-noindex if a gas customer-charge article exists elsewhere.

4. content/terms.md — the weakest trust page. 32 lines, generic HTML paragraphs, 'Effective date: 2024-12-01' while front matter claims updated 2026-08-03; no jurisdiction/dispute clause, no affiliate/advertising terms despite the site monetizing via AdSense and Amazon. For a money-adjacent (YMYL) site this is a real E-E-A-T gap. Recommendation: improve-and-retain — add disputes, jurisdiction, commercial relationships, and align dates.

5. content/author/margaret-harrington.md (representative of all 5 author profiles) — 23-line stubs that explicitly disclaim individual credentials ('It identifies the desk responsible for guides...'). Combined with identical 'AI assistance' boilerplate on all five profiles, these pages add minimal E-E-A-T value. The honest desk framing is better than fabrication, but the profiles should carry at least one concrete example guide and a real source per desk. Recommendation: improve-and-retain.
